title: Applied ML Evals: Unified Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization, and Regression Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook unifies the Applied ML & Evals team's standard practices for: eval harness onboarding, prompt set and benchmark management, model onboarding checklists, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, evaluation engineers, model owners, and SREs who operate or validate models on Redwood’s inference platform.

Goals
- Provide a single, prescriptive workflow that reduces onboarding time for new models and experiments.
- Ensure consistent prompt sets and benchmarks are used for quality comparisons.
- Define minimum quality guardrails to prevent regressions in production.
- Standardize quantization profile creation and validation for safe cost/latency optimizations.
- Capture a clear regression triage flow that balances impact, rollback, and remediation.

Scope and applicability
- Applies to: open or customer-provided foundation models being evaluated for Redwood hosting or recommended model variants used in Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Not in scope: research-only prototypes that will not be deployed; experiment notebooks without CI-backed harness integration.

Owners and roles
- Playbook owner: Applied ML & Evals team (process steward: Aisha Patel)
- Model owner: engineering team that owns the consumer of the model (responsible for prompt definitions and acceptance criteria)
- Eval harness owner: Eval engineering (maintains CI jobs, baseline metrics, and tooling)
- SRE liaison: Eng SRE (capacity & rollout guidance)
- Release approver: Product + Applied ML lead (for production model additions and quantization rollouts)

High-level workflow (end-to-end)
1. Intake and scoping (Model Owner)
   - Submit model onboarding request via the internal catalog form (link: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding). Include model architecture, HF repo/weights link, expected tokenization, and target workloads.
   - Add initial evaluation goals: primary metrics (e.g., EM, F1, ROUGE, embedding similarity), latency targets (p50/p95), and cost targets.
2. Eval harness integration (Eval engineering)
   - Add model to eval harness with a config YAML: model_id, tokenizer, entrypoint, sequence_length_bins, and quantization candidates.
   - Create CI job to run baseline suites (see section: Standard CI suites).
3. Prompt set and benchmark selection (Cross-functional)
   - Select curated prompt sets from the catalog: unit prompts, end-to-end application prompts, adversarial negatives, and safety prompts.
   - Define gold/reference outputs and evaluation scripts (deterministic for unit tests, seed-controlled where sampling used).
4. Quantization and performance testing (Applied ML)
   - Generate quantization profiles following the Quantization Guidance section. Run functional tests and evaluate quality drift vs. float baseline.
5. Guardrails and SLO pairing (Prod/SRE/Product)
   - Map evaluation metrics to guardrail thresholds and SLOs. Approve rollout plan and canary policies.
6. Regression triage & post-deployment monitoring (All)
   - Monitor eval-run metrics and user-facing quality signals. If regression detected, follow Regression Triage Playbook.

Standard CI suites
- smoke: lightweight deterministic tests (latency smoke and basic correctness on 20 prompts). Run on PRs.
- baseline: full evaluation against prompt set catalog (recommended cadence: nightly). Computes primary metrics and stores artifacts.
- perf: latency/cost profiling with a representative request mix and sequence length distribution. Scheduled weekly or pre-release.
- quant-verify: runs quantized binary against float baseline for the stable quantization candidates.

Required artifacts for model onboarding
- model-metadata.json (schema): model_id, architecture, tokenizer, vocab_size, checkpoint_sha, float_cpu_eval_metrics, recommended_sequence_lengths. (Attach to onboarding ticket as a file.)
- prompt-set zip: contains canonical prompts, categories, and reference outputs (where applicable).
- eval-config.yaml: harness config used to run CI (no nested objects beyond YAML allowed in the catalog; store as a single file).
- quant-profiles/ directory: candidate profiles and validation logs.

Prompt set and benchmark management
Guidelines
- Canonical prompt sets must be categorized: unit, e2e, adversarial, safety, and customer-simulated.
- Each prompt entry must contain: id, category, input_text, expected_output (if deterministic), and tags indicating language, domain, and length bucket.
- Maintain a test coverage matrix that maps prompt sets to product features (maintain in the catalog spreadsheet).
- Version control: Prompt sets are versioned with semantic versions (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Changes that alter expected behavior increment MAJOR.
Examples and best practices
- Use short, focused prompts for unit tests to isolate failure modes.
- Use longer, multi-turn sequences for E2E benchmark scenarios.
- For embedding quality, include a labeled similarity dataset or contrastive pairs and measure cosine AUC and mean avg precision.

Quality guardrails (policy + thresholds)
- Primary quality metrics: task-specific accuracy (EM/F1), output toxicity rate, hallucination rate (measured vs. knowledge ground truth), and embedding retrieval MRR.
- Minimum acceptance thresholds (example template):
  - Task accuracy (EM/F1): >= previous stable model - 2% absolute or >= absolute 70% (team-owned)
  - Embedding MRR: >= previous stable model - 0.03 absolute
  - Toxicity rate: <= previous stable model + 0.5% absolute and below product maximum (0.5% by default)
  - Latency (p95): must meet model-specific latency SLO (see perf profile)
- Blocking criteria for production: any regression that fails the above thresholds after canary analysis must be remediated or rolled back.
- Alerting: CI baseline failures should create tickets and annotate the model catalog entry. Production drift beyond rolling window thresholds triggers incident process.

Quantization profiles and validation
Objective
- Reduce inference cost and/or latency while keeping quality within guardrails.
Profile creation process
1. Candidate selection: identify per-layer and per-tensor quantization candidates based on model architecture and perf targets.
2. Calibration set: use a 1-5k representative prompt sample (drawn from the prompt catalog in the intended domain).
3. Quantize and run quant-verify suite vs. float baseline. Capture metric deltas and per-prompt diffs.
4. Thresholding: reject candidates that cause metric degradation > allowed delta (default 1.5% relative for task metrics or absolute 0.02 for embedding MRR).
5. Canary rollout: start with internal canary traffic (1-2% traffic) with close monitoring of user-facing indicators and eval harness benchmarks.
Validation artifacts to produce
- quant-profile.json (name, date, transform details, quant-type, bits per tensor, per-layer notes)
- quant-validation-report.md (diffs, top failing prompts, suggested mitigations)
- perf-and-cost-report.csv (latency, p50/p95, cost-per-request estimate)

Regression triage playbook
Trigger conditions
- Any CI baseline failure for a production model.
- Production alerts: user complaints, automated quality drift signals, or safety filter rate spikes.
Triage steps
1. Acknowledge and classify (Triage lead)
   - Severity levels: Sev-1 (customer-facing outage or major quality regression), Sev-2 (noticeable regression for a segment), Sev-3 (minor degradation or noisy CI flake).
   - Assign owner: model owner + eval engineer.
2. Reproduce locally (Eval engineer)
   - Run the same eval harness with the failing seeds and prompt IDs; collect environment metadata (model checksum, quant-profile id, runtime flags).
   - Re-run float baseline to exclude harness flakiness.
3. Root cause hypothesis (Cross-functional)
   - Common root causes: prompt changes, model checkout mismatch, tokenizer mismatch, quantization artifact, config drift (sequence-length bins), or dataset regression.
   - Use differential report to find top N failing prompts and the nature of errors (omissions, hallucinations, format breaks).
4. Immediate remediation options
   - Roll back to previous model/quant profile in production (fastest for Sev-1).
   - Apply prompt or post-processing fix for format-only regressions (short-term).
   - Create hotfix eval with adjusted quant params and run quant-verify.
5. Postmortem and preventive actions
   - For Sev-1/Sev-2, complete a blameless postmortem within 7 days documenting timeline, RCA, and action items.
   - Update prompt sets, CI guards, and quant profiles as needed.

Testing checklist (pre-release gate)
- All CI suites green for 3 consecutive runs.
- Quant-verify showing no blocking regressions.
- Perf suite meets expected p50/p95 targets.
- Canary run plan and rollback playbook documented.
- Observability: dashboards added/updated (cost, latency, key metric deltas), and alert thresholds configured.

Operational considerations and SRE coordination
- Capacity planning: model owners must provide expected QPS and sequence length distribution. Work with GPU Fleet team to reserve Dedicated capacity when expected sustained QPS > 300 rps per model.
- Autoscaling knobs: confirm batch sizing constraints and max-inflight-requests.
- Fallback policies: configure automatic fallback to a lower-cost or lower-latency model variant if p95 latency breaches SLO for > 3 minutes.

Appendix: Quick commands and diagnostic snippets
- Run baseline suite locally: 
  ./eval-harness/run.sh --config eval-config.yaml --model-dir /models/my-model --out results/
- Generate quant profile (example):
  python tools/quantize.py --checkpoint ckpt.pt --calibration samples/calib.jsonl --out quant-profiles/q1.json
- Diff float vs quant summary (example):
  jq -r '.metrics | to_entries[] | "\(.key): float=\(.value.float) quant=\(.value.quant) delta=\(.value.delta)"' results/diff.json
